uncited: It builds on [Local illumination, shadows and ambient occlusion](34-local-illumination-shadows-and-ambient-occlusion.md) by evaluating visibility and illumination at a surface point $\mathbf{p}$ using a heightfield representation.
If $NdotL > 0$, trace a shadow ray starting from $\mathbf{p}_{start} = (p_x + n_x \cdot \text{bias}, p_y + \text{bias}, p_z + n_z \cdot \text{bias})$ with jitter.
Let the result be `shadow` (1.0 if unshadowed, 0.0 if shadowed).
Get the cloud shadow factor: `cloudShade = cloudShadowAt(p.x, p.z, p.y)`.
- **Self-Shadowing:** Failing to bias the shadow ray origin results in severe self-shadowing artifacts on coarse heightfields.
- **Normal Interpolation:** Using finite differences on a bilinear heightfield produces piecewise constant normals, causing visible facet edges.
